title: cross-sdk session handoff + ergonomic stream helpers (go v1.5.3)
author: Ava Morales
description: Implements a Go-side counterpart of the cross-sdk session handoff protocol (session-handoff-v2) used to rotate credentials for long-lived streaming connections without breaking consumer code. Motivation: existing stream reauth patterns were SDK-specific and caused duplicated logic, unexpected reconnects, and inconsistent backoff between languages. This PR: 1) introduces a ConnectionHandoff interface that exposes a simple, documented contract for credential injection during active streams; 2) adds ergonomic StreamClient helpers (StreamContext, WithAutoRefresh) so callers can opt into zero-boilerplate token refresh and backpressure-friendly reconnection; 3) centralizes adaptive backoff profiles to match the TypeScript and Python defaults and includes a compatibility shim for older servers; 4) bumps the Go SDK to v1.5.3 with CHANGELOG entries and migration notes; 5) adds unit and integration tests that exercise handshake edge cases (mid-stream refresh, race with Close), plus a small docs section under docs/streaming.md. Checklist: - [x] design doc sync with SDK leads (link: https://linear.app/ENG-2345) - [x] cross-lang protocol spec reviewed - [x] go unit tests added - [x] integration test against redwood-internal mock server - [x] docs and changelog updated - [x] version bump and release notes. Notes on compatibility: the new ConnectionHandoff is opt-in; default behavior unchanged for existing callers. This PR is intentionally scoped to the client surface and avoids runtime/server changes; server migration is tracked separately (ENG-2389).

7e3b91f: add StreamClient convenience constructors and WithAutoRefresh option

c6d8a12: integration tests against mock reauth server
review_comments: Jordan Liu (reviewer): Overall this looks good; please add a short benchmark that simulates 100 concurrent streams to ensure the auto-refresh goroutine is bounded.
Ava Morales (author reply): Added a micro-benchmark and documented the goroutine lifecycle in stream_client.go; it lives in the same worker pool and is reclaimed on Close(), see commit 48a2d43.
Priya Shah (reviewer): Can we make the backoff profile configurable through the client options? Right now the defaults match other SDKs but customers will want to tweak.
Ava Morales (author reply): Exposed BackoffProfile as an option on StreamClient; kept the default preset but added docs and examples.
Samir Patel (reviewer): Flaky integration test observed on first CI run (race on handshake). Suggest using a deterministic handshake delay in the mock server.
Ava Morales (author reply): Fixed race by introducing handshake lock in mock and added a deterministic mode for CI; rerun CI.
release_notes: Client: Added ConnectionHandoff interface and StreamClient.WithAutoRefresh to support non-disruptive token rotation for long-lived streams. Backwards compatible; opt-in. SDK: bumped to v1.5.3. Bugfixes: handshake race fix in mock server used by tests.
notes_for_release: Migration: no changes required for existing users. To opt-in to automatic in-stream credential refresh, construct StreamClient using WithAutoRefresh(tokenProvider) and ensure tokenProvider returns refreshed tokens when called. See docs/streaming.md examples.
security_implications: no direct secrets landing; this PR adds a token provider callback pattern which does not persist secrets. Ensure user-supplied token providers follow secure storage practices.
testing_summary: Added 12 unit tests and 2 integration scenarios covering mid-stream refresh, concurrent refreshes, and Close() races. Also added a micro-benchmark simulating 100 concurrent streams to validate goroutine bounding and latency impact.
